criterion: The signup card on the front surface asks for a birthday above the username field.
evaluation_rule: The BIRTHDAY field is the group of three month, day and year selects. Yes if those three selects sit above the username input on the signup card. No if the username input sits above them, or if the birthday selects are absent.

criterion: The marketplace list names the member who published each item beside a Kredz price.
evaluation_rule: KREDZ is the platform's virtual currency, so a price reads as a number of Kredz. Yes if every row of the marketplace list shows a publisher name next to a Kredz price. No if any row shows a price with no publisher name.

criterion: The Kredz surface shows the balance rising by the pack size once a pack purchase finishes.
evaluation_rule: A PACK is one of the three bundles of Kredz sold for money, each advertising the number of Kredz it carries. Yes if the balance shown after a purchase is higher by exactly the advertised number. No if the balance is unchanged, or moves by a different amount.

criterion: The payout surface lists six eligibility conditions, each carrying a met or unmet marker of its own.
evaluation_rule: Yes if six separate conditions appear, each with its own met or unmet marker. No if fewer than six appear, or if one combined verdict stands in for them.

criterion: A refused action on the marketplace leaves the visitor on the same surface with a reason shown.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a refused purchase keeps the visitor where they were and shows a sentence giving the reason. No if the surface changes, or if the refusal is silent.

criterion: An empty list on the creator dashboard shows a sentence naming what would fill the list.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a list holding nothing shows a sentence describing what would appear there. No if the empty list shows a blank region or a bare dash.

criterion: The marketplace surface gives its primary action a stronger blue fill than every other control there.
evaluation_rule: Yes if one control on the marketplace surface carries a clearly stronger blue fill than the rest. No if two controls share the strongest fill, or if every control looks alike.

criterion: A reserved message slot sits under each signup field before any message appears there.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the space below every signup field is held open on an untouched form, so a later message moves nothing below it. No if the fields sit flush and a message pushes the content under them downwards.

criterion: On the charts surface a loading placeholder stays visually separate from loaded content under a reduced-motion preference.
evaluation_rule: A LOADING PLACEHOLDER is the grey block standing in for content still arriving. Yes if the placeholder still reads as an unfinished region once motion is reduced. No if a held placeholder looks the same as real content.

criterion: A skip link appears at the top of the surface the first time keyboard focus enters the document.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the first tab press reveals a visible control that jumps past the navigation to the main region. No if no such control appears on the first tab press.

criterion: The header search stays reachable at a phone-width viewport on the charts surface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a search input, or an icon that opens one, is present at phone width. No if the search vanishes entirely at that width.

criterion: A comment box or a message thread appears on a marketplace item surface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if any commenting or messaging control appears on an item surface. No if the item surface carries none.

criterion: A purchase confirmation appears on the Kredz surface with the balance still showing the earlier figure.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a success message is shown with no matching movement in the balance. No if every success message is accompanied by the balance change it claims.

criterion: Switching the footer language selector on the charts surface changes the wording in the navigation bar.
evaluation_rule: Yes if choosing a second language rewrites the navigation, the footer and the page headings. No if any of those stays in the first language.
